description: Baseline: locked real-config soak benchmark and correctness gates

asi.hypothesis: Establish stable real-config CPU baseline while preserving 90 ms cadence and visual behavior.
asi.workload: Three 3-second Snacks dashboard soaks after 1-second warmup; median CPU; default grudge_axe glitch; 10-13 FPS gate.
asi.anti_cheat: Benchmark and checks locked; cadence, timer cleanup, generation, and lifecycle behavior enforced.
asi.finding: Baseline CPU 4.975%; full redraw p95 7.122 ms; section serialization 798.5 µs and 146.1 KiB/call.

description: Cache filtered color results across animation frames

asi.hypothesis: Source/filter color pairs repeat across frames; memoizing exact tint results removes repeated RGB parsing, luminance math, and formatting without changing output.
asi.finding: CPU improved 16.4%; section mean fell from 798.5 µs to 203.2 µs. Allocation stayed ~146 KiB because section tables/strings still rebuild. Full-update p95 rose, likely soak noise or GC variance; cadence unchanged.
asi.next_action: Target section table/string reconstruction while preserving exact frame content and full redraw cadence.
asi.anti_cheat: Exact color function output cached by inputs; no frame skipping, cadence change, or benchmark edit.

description: Cache highlight names by filtered color and glow

asi.hypothesis: Each segment rebuilds the same highlight-name string; caching exact color/glow to name mappings removes repeated concatenation and lookup work.
asi.finding: Section mean fell another 38.4% from 203.2 µs to 125.1 µs. Primary CPU improved only 0.8% versus prior keep, likely near noise; redraw p95 recovered somewhat. Allocation metric unchanged, implying table/text construction now dominates.
asi.next_action: Measure a structural reduction in section text table/string allocation; avoid more tiny lookup tweaks.
asi.anti_cheat: Highlight semantics and names unchanged; cadence and full Snacks redraw preserved.

description: Reuse Snacks section and text entry tables

asi.hypothesis: Snacks consumes section text synchronously without mutating source entries, so reusing section and entry tables removes per-frame table allocation while preserving exact strings/highlights.
asi.finding: CPU improved 2.8% versus prior keep. Section allocation dropped from 145.8 KiB/call to ~0.001 KiB and mean improved 6.9%. Remaining section cost is string concatenation and traversal; full redraw still dominates.
asi.safety: Snacks block formatting creates child tables via metatables and reads source text; it does not mutate source entries. Generation/lifecycle checks and timer/FPS gates passed.
asi.next_action: Reduce repeated per-segment traversal/string concatenation using cacheable serialized rows, then validate real CPU.

description: Cache serialized row variants by segments and effect color

asi.hypothesis: Caching immutable serialized row variants should remove per-segment work after warmup and lower real dashboard CPU.
asi.finding: Micro section mean collapsed from 116.5 µs to 3.9 µs, but primary CPU worsened 0.85% and max RSS rose 5.1%. Full Snacks redraw dominates enough that a large persistent row cache does not pay back in the real workload.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed and memory cost increased; this is benchmark-local over-optimization with no real workload win.
asi.next_action_hint: Stop optimizing section microbenchmark. Target work inside or around full Snacks redraw, especially avoiding redundant static dashboard recomputation without reducing delivered visual frames.

description: Cache active dashboard buffer to avoid repeated window scans

asi.hypothesis: Caching the active dashboard buffer should remove one all-window scan from each timer tick while retaining fallback discovery and cleanup.
asi.finding: Primary CPU worsened 7.3%. The scan is not material in the real workload, and section calls without a visible dashboard repeatedly attempted discovery, adding diagnostic allocation.
asi.rollback_reason: Clear primary regression with no compensating benefit.
asi.next_action_hint: Avoid lifecycle/window-scan micro-optimizations. Profile full redraw subphases or test smaller output representation changes.

description: Noise calibration rerun of current best

asi.hypothesis: Repeat current best unchanged to estimate run-to-run noise before pursuing riskier architecture changes.
asi.finding: CPU varied from 4.010% to 4.128% (+2.9%) with identical code; update p95 varied inversely. Future gains below ~3% need confirmation runs.
asi.rollback_reason: No code change and metric did not improve stored best.
asi.next_action_hint: Prioritize experiments expected to exceed 3% CPU improvement; confirm marginal wins before retaining complexity.

asi.hypothesis: Nested source->filter cache lookup avoids constructing and hashing a concatenated key for every segment while retaining exact memoized results.
asi.finding: CPU improved 3.25% versus stored best, just above measured ~3% run noise. Section mean improved 33.6% from 116.5 µs to 77.4 µs, providing a consistent causal signal. Cadence and memory held.
asi.next_action: Apply the same nested-key strategy to highlight-name cache, then require a real CPU win rather than relying on microbenchmark alone.
asi.anti_cheat: Only cache indexing changed; output, redraw count, and cadence unchanged.

asi.hypothesis: Nested color->glow lookup should avoid highlight cache key concatenation, mirroring the filtered-color cache win.
asi.finding: Primary CPU regressed 3.2% and section mean was unchanged. Highlight keys are already final color strings and concatenation/interning is cheaper than an extra nested lookup here.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regression at roughly the measured noise threshold with no diagnostic improvement.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not generalize cache structures blindly. Keep nested cache only for source/filter tinting, where section timing proved the benefit.

description: Cache final highlight names per segment and filter

asi.hypothesis: A weak per-segment cache of final highlight names should fuse tint and highlight lookups for stable ANSI segments.
asi.finding: CPU regressed 8.1%, section mean worsened 9.1%, and RSS increased. Per-segment variant-table lookup and cache footprint cost more than the already-fast nested tint cache plus global highlight cache.
asi.rollback_reason: Strong primary and memory regression; extra cache layer is counterproductive.
asi.next_action_hint: Current hot section path is sufficiently optimized. Investigate reducing Snacks-render input complexity or accept architecture boundary as next ceiling.

description: Track line boundaries instead of searching newline strings

asi.hypothesis: Tracking the current line start should replace a per-segment string search used only to prevent cross-line merging.
asi.finding: CPU regressed 5.4% and section mean regressed 25.5%. Lua numeric/branch bookkeeping was slower than the optimized C string search on these short cached strings, or amplified JIT instability.
asi.rollback_reason: Both primary and targeted diagnostic regressed clearly.
asi.next_action_hint: Retain the simple newline find. Avoid replacing optimized C library operations with Lua branches without evidence.

description: Use numeric loops in Snacks section serialization

asi.hypothesis: Numeric loops should reduce iterator overhead in the 1,000-segment section hot path.
asi.finding: Section mean improved 6.1%, but primary CPU worsened 1.9%, inside measured noise and with no real-workload evidence. Whole redraw remains dominant.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary did not improve; micro-only gain is insufficient under anti-overfitting rule.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not keep section-loop tweaks without confirmed real CPU benefit. Consider a confirmation only if combined with a structural redraw improvement, not standalone.

name: Reduce dashboard logo redraw load with frame-aware measurement

description: Frame-aware baseline separating animation ticks from full redraws

asi.hypothesis: Separate generated animation frame rate from full Snacks redraw rate before evaluating incremental rendering.
asi.finding: Frame-aware baseline: 4.133% CPU, 11.223 delivered FPS, 11.223 full redraw FPS. Instrumentation preserves prior workload while enabling honest measurement of equivalent non-redraw visual updates.
asi.measurement_change: Added generic on_frame callback and redraw_fps metric. FPS gate now tracks generated frames, not User update events. Correctness test requires callback activity.
asi.anti_cheat: Change made and baselined before structural optimization; full redraw rate remains independently visible.

description: Animate stable highlight groups and redraw only geometry changes

asi.hypothesis: Stable line/shade highlight groups can animate color-only frames through nvim_set_hl and reserve full Snacks redraws for geometry glitches.
asi.finding: Full redraw rate fell from 11.22 to 4.95 FPS and redraw p95 halved, but CPU exploded from 4.13% to 10.12%. Hundreds of nvim_set_hl calls per frame cost more than Snacks buffer/extmark rebuilds. RSS fell because fewer redraw allocations, but CPU is decisive.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary CPU regressed 145%; direct highlight redefinition is the wrong rendering primitive at this group cardinality.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not pursue per-line/per-shade highlight animation. A viable incremental renderer would need far fewer mutable groups or direct batched extmark updates; record as deferred architecture work.
